## The question

How can a short, reproducible Python analysis become a shareable web report?

- Make a deterministic toy price history.
- Estimate parameters from its returns.
- Simulate and compare paths.
- Render the same story with Quarto.

## The data

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "src")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from market_demo import generate_prices, log_returns, estimate_parameters, simulate_gbm

prices = generate_prices()
returns = log_returns(prices)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.plot(prices.index, prices, color="#2878B5")
ax.set(title="Five years of synthetic daily prices", xlabel="Date", ylabel="Price")
ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## The calibration

```{python}
estimates = estimate_parameters(returns)
print(f"Observations: {len(returns):,}")
print(f"Annualized drift: {estimates['drift']:.1%}")
print(f"Annualized volatility: {estimates['volatility']:.1%}")
```

Daily log-return volatility is annualized with \(\sqrt{252}\).

## The comparison

```{python}
paths = simulate_gbm(
    initial_price=float(prices.iloc[0]),
    n_days=len(returns),
    drift=estimates["drift"],
    volatility=estimates["volatility"],
)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
ax.plot(range(len(prices)), prices.to_numpy(), color="#2878B5", label="Synthetic history")
ax.plot(paths.index, paths.median(axis=1), color="#E15759", label="Simulated median")
ax.fill_between(
    paths.index,
    paths.quantile(0.05, axis=1),
    paths.quantile(0.95, axis=1),
    color="#F28E2B",
    alpha=0.2,
    label="Simulated 5th–95th percentile",
)
ax.set(title="One path versus calibrated simulations", xlabel="Trading day", ylabel="Price")
ax.legend(frameon=False)
ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## What Quarto adds

- One source format can produce a website, a dashboard, and slides.
- Code and results stay together and are re-executed on render.
- The same analysis functions can also be imported by a Jupyter notebook.

This is a teaching example with synthetic data, not an investment model.
